preview.tournamentOverview: Detroit Golf Club rewards ball-striking over putting, with off-the-tee and approach play carrying the heaviest course weights. The Rocket Classic is a mid-tier PGA Tour stop that draws a weaker field, creating value opportunities for in-form players who excel in the key statistical categories.
preview.modelExplainer: SG OTT (26.8%) and SG Total (22.8%) dominate the model, followed by SG APP (21.3%). SG ATG (10.6%) and SG PUTT (8.4%) receive lower weight, while Driving Accuracy (4.1%), Bogey Avoidance (3.0%), and Birdie/Bogey Ratio (3.0%) round out the remaining influence.
preview.pickApproach: We tier bets by combining tournament rank with power rank, prioritizing players who rank high in both. Top targets show strong SG OTT and SG APP marks that align with course demands, while avoiding players whose putting or around-the-green numbers drag down their overall profile.

article.title: Rocket Classic 2026: Model Ranks Detroit Fit at Detroit Golf Club
article.dek: Tournament model identifies Cameron Young, Si Woo Kim, and Jake Knapp as the strongest course fits for the 147-player field at Detroit Golf Club.
article.introduction: The Rocket Classic model weights off-the-tee (26.8%) and approach (21.3%) most heavily at Detroit Golf Club. Cameron Young leads the model at rank 1 with 1.574 SG Total, while Si Woo Kim sits at rank 2 with 1.236 SG Total. The 147-player field tees off July 30 with no weather or tee-time data available.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: The Rocket Classic model ranks Cameron Young 1st, Si Woo Kim 2nd, and Jake Knapp 3rd for the 147-player field at Detroit Golf Club. Course weights place SG OTT at 26.8% and SG APP at 21.3%, making driving and approach play the primary factors. The model places 20 players above 0.5 SG Total, with Cameron Young leading at 1.574.

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: Detroit Golf Club's weighting favors SG OTT (26.8%) and SG APP (21.3%) over putting (8.4%). Cameron Young leads the model with 0.699 SG OTT and 0.499 SG APP. Si Woo Kim ranks 2nd with 0.572 SG OTT and 0.912 SG APP, the strongest approach mark among the top 5. Jake Knapp ranks 3rd with 0.264 SG OTT and 0.342 SG APP but leads the top 10 with 1.285 SG Putt.

sections.heading: Recent Form
sections.body: The model incorporates four tracked rounds for Cameron Young, Si Woo Kim, Russell Henley, Hideki Matsuyama, Chris Gotterup, Ryo Hisatsune, Jacob Bridgeman, Xander Schauffele, Ryan Gerard, Patrick Cantlay, and Rickie Fowler. Jake Knapp, Nicolai Højgaard, and Harris English have two tracked rounds each. Jordan Spieth also has two tracked rounds.

sections.heading: Post-Open Workload
sections.body: Four-round workload players include Cameron Young, Si Woo Kim, Russell Henley, Hideki Matsuyama, Chris Gotterup, Ryo Hisatsune, Jacob Bridgeman, Xander Schauffele, Ryan Gerard, Patrick Cantlay, and Rickie Fowler. Two-round workload players include Jake Knapp, Nicolai Højgaard, Harris English, and Jordan Spieth. The model does not classify workload as positive or negative on its own.

sections.heading: FedExCup Motivation
sections.body: Cameron Young enters at FedExCup rank 3, Si Woo Kim at rank 7, and Chris Gotterup at rank 5. Russell Henley sits at rank 14, Jacob Bridgeman at rank 13, and Xander Schauffele at rank 15. Jordan Spieth enters at rank 55, the only player among the selected picks outside the top 50.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: Cameron Young, Si Woo Kim, Chris Gotterup, Ryo Hisatsune, and Xander Schauffele combine top-10 model rank with skipped Scottish Open participation. Jake Knapp and Nicolai Højgaard combine strong model rank with two tracked rounds after missing the Open cut. Ryan Gerard, Patrick Cantlay, Rickie Fowler, and Harris English show model rank well ahead of power rank.

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: Si Woo Kim ranks 2nd in the model with 1.236 SG Total and 0.912 SG APP but carries -0.39 SG Putt, the weakest putting mark among the top 5. Nicolai Højgaard ranks 8th with 1.568 SG Total and 0.712 SG APP but missed the Open cut with two tracked rounds. Russell Henley ranks 11th with 1.186 SG Total and 0.537 SG Putt but has the lowest SG APP (0.313) among the top 12. Hideki Matsuyama ranks 12th with 1.197 SG Total but has the lowest SG OTT (-0.099) among the top 15.

Russell Henley ranks 11th with 1.186 SG Total and 0.537 SG Putt.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: Cameron Young leads the model at rank 1 with 1.574 SG Total and 0.699 SG OTT. Jake Knapp ranks 3rd with 2.002 SG Total and 1.285 SG Putt but has 0.264 SG OTT, 15th among the top 10. Jacob Bridgeman ranks 4th with 1.933 SG Total and 1.339 SG Putt but has -0.152 SG ATG. Xander Schauffele ranks 5th with 1.443 SG Total and 0.662 SG APP but has 0.423 SG OTT, 8th among the top 10. Nicolai Højgaard ranks 8th with 1.568 SG Total and 0.712 SG APP but has 0.256 SG OTT, 14th among the top 10.

sections.heading: Top-20 Targets
sections.body: Russell Henley ranks 11th with 1.186 SG Total and 0.537 SG Putt but has 0.313 SG APP, 15th among the top 20. Hideki Matsuyama ranks 12th with 1.197 SG Total and 0.635 SG APP but has -0.099 SG OTT. Ryan Gerard ranks 13th with 0.94 SG Total and 0.712 SG APP but has -0.276 SG ATG. Patrick Cantlay ranks 14th with 0.772 SG Total and 0.437 SG OTT but has 0.146 SG APP, 19th among the top 20. Rickie Fowler ranks 18th with 0.679 SG Total and 0.589 SG Putt but has 0.111 SG APP, 20th among the top 20. Harris English ranks 19th with 0.7 SG Total and 0.627 SG Putt but has -0.214 SG APP. Jordan Spieth ranks 23rd with 0.465 SG Total and 0.501 SG OTT but has -0.053 SG OTT.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are not available. Workload coverage includes only recorded rounds from The Open Championship and Genesis Scottish Open. Opposite-field, DP World Tour, LIV, and other events may be missing, so 'No tracked rounds' does not necessarily mean the player rested.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Strong model-supported bets: Cameron Young (rank 1), Si Woo Kim (rank 2), Jake Knapp (rank 3). Secondary value plays: Jacob Bridgeman (rank 4), Xander Schauffele (rank 5), Chris Gotterup (rank 6), Ryo Hisatsune (rank 7). Speculative long shots: Ryan Gerard (rank 13), Patrick Cantlay (rank 14), Rickie Fowler (rank 18), Harris English (rank 19), Jordan Spieth (rank 23).

article.conclusion: Strong model-supported bets: Cameron Young, Si Woo Kim, Jake Knapp. Secondary value plays: Jacob Bridgeman, Xander Schauffele, Chris Gotterup, Ryo Hisatsune. Speculative long shots: Ryan Gerard, Patrick Cantlay, Rickie Fowler, Harris English, Jordan Spieth.
